meta.blurb: Yer o'lchovchi K. qorli qishloqqa keladi — tepalikdagi Qasr uni chaqirgan, lekin u yerga yetib borishning iloji yo'q. Kafkaning so'nggi, tugallanmagan romani: byurokratiya, yolg'izlik va «qabul qilinish» uchun cheksiz kurash.
meta.why_uz: «Metamorfoza» va «Jarayon»dan keyin Kafkaning eng muhim asari. Kamyu «Sizif afsonasi»da aynan «Qasr»ni tahlil qilgan — javondagi Kamyu asarlari bilan birga o'qish juda qiziq. Gaplari uzun, lekin tili tushunarli: B2–C1 darajasi uchun yaxshi mashq.
meta.author_uz: Frans Kafka (1883–1924) — Pragada tug'ilgan nemis tilli yozuvchi. Hayotligida juda kam asar nashr etgan; vasiyatida qo'lyozmalarini yoqib yuborishni so'ragan, lekin do'sti Maks Brod ularni nashr qildi. «Qasr» 1922-yilda yozilgan va 1926-yilda, Kafka vafotidan keyin chop etilgan.
meta.edition_uz: To'liq matn. Inglizcha matn — WordDrop'ning nemischa asl nusxadan («Das Schloß», Kafka vafotidan keyin Maks Brod nashri asosidagi matn) o'z tarjimasi; mashhur Muir (1930), Harman (1998) va Underwood (1997) tarjimalaridan foydalanilmagan, chunki ular hali himoyada. O'zbekchasi qo'lda tarjima qilingan. Kafka romanni tugatmagan — matn gap o'rtasida uziladi. Kafka bob nomlari qo'ymagan, bu nashrdagi bo'linish va sarlavhalar WordDrop'niki; juda uzun xatboshilar o'qish qulayligi uchun bo'lingan. Nashr bosqichma-bosqich to'ldirilmoqda. Muqova — foydalanuvchi bergan rasm.
meta.progress_uz: Hozircha 22 bobdan 3 tasi tayyor; qolganlari bosqichma-bosqich qo'shiladi.
meta.source_uz: Frans Kafka 1924-yilda vafot etgan — nemischa asl matn jamoat mulki.

chapters.title: 1. Arrival
chapters.recap_uz: K. qorli tunda qishloqqa keladi va mehmonxonada somon to'shakda uxlaydi. Kastelyanning o'g'li Shvartser uni ruxsatsiz tunagani uchun haydamoqchi bo'ladi; K. o'zini graf chaqirgan yer o'lchovchi deb ataydi. Qasr telefon orqali avval rad etadi, keyin uni «yer o'lchovchi» deb tan oladi. Ertasi kuni K. Qasr tomon yuradi, lekin ko'cha unga hech qachon yaqinlashmaydi; o'qituvchi bilan g'alati suhbat, ko'nchi Lazemanning uyida dam olish va «Qasrdan kelgan qiz».

paras.en: It was late at night when K. arrived. The village lay under deep snow. Of the Castle hill nothing could be seen; mist and darkness wrapped it round, and not even the faintest glimmer of light hinted at the great Castle. For a long while K. stood on the wooden bridge that led from the high road into the village and gazed upward into what seemed an emptiness.
paras.uz: K. yetib kelganida tun yarmidan oshgan edi. Qishloq qalin qor ostida yotardi. Qasr tepaligidan hech narsa ko'rinmasdi; uni tuman va zulmat o'rab olgan, hatto eng xira nur ham ulkan Qasr borligiga ishora qilmasdi. K. katta yo'ldan qishloqqa olib boradigan yog'och ko'prikda uzoq turdi va bo'shliqdek tuyulgan tepalikka tikilib qoldi.

paras.en: Then he went to look for a place to sleep. At the inn they were still up; the landlord had no room to let, but, greatly surprised and flustered by so late a guest, he was willing to let K. sleep on a straw sack in the taproom. K. agreed. A few peasants were still sitting over their beer, but he did not want to talk to anyone; he fetched the straw sack from the loft himself and lay down near the stove. It was warm, the peasants were quiet, he looked them over a little with tired eyes, and then he fell asleep.
paras.uz: Keyin u tunash uchun joy izlab ketdi. Mehmonxonada hali uxlashmagan edi; mehmonxona egasining ijaraga beradigan xonasi yo'q edi, lekin u bunday kech kelgan mehmondan juda hayron va sarosimaga tushib, K.ga umumiy zalda somon to'shakda uxlashga ruxsat berishga rozi bo'ldi. K. rozi bo'ldi. Bir necha dehqon hali pivo ichib o'tirardi, lekin u hech kim bilan gaplashishni istamadi; somon to'shakni chordoqdan o'zi olib tushdi va pechka yoniga yotdi. Iliq edi, dehqonlar jim edi; u charchagan ko'zlari bilan ularni biroz kuzatdi-da, uxlab qoldi.

paras.en: But only a short time later he was woken. A young man in town clothes, with an actor's face, narrow eyes and heavy eyebrows, was standing beside him with the landlord. The peasants were still there too; some had turned their chairs round to see and hear better. The young man apologized very politely for having woken K., introduced himself as the son of the Castle steward, and then said: 'This village belongs to the Castle. Whoever lives or spends the night here lives or spends the night, in a manner of speaking, in the Castle. Nobody may do that without the Count's permission. But you have no such permission, or at least you have not shown it.'
paras.uz: Lekin oradan ko'p o'tmay uni uyg'otishdi. Shaharcha kiyingan, aktyornikidek yuzli, ko'zlari qisiq, qoshlari quyuq bir yigit mehmonxona egasi bilan yonida turardi. Dehqonlar ham hali o'sha yerda edi; ba'zilari yaxshiroq ko'rish va eshitish uchun stullarini burib olgan edi. Yigit K.ni uyg'otgani uchun juda xushmuomalalik bilan uzr so'radi, o'zini Qasr kastelyanining (qasr nozirining) o'g'li deb tanishtirdi va keyin dedi: «Bu qishloq Qasrning mulki. Bu yerda yashagan yoki tunagan odam, bir ma'noda, Qasrda yashaydi yoki tunaydi. Grafning ruxsatisiz hech kim buni qila olmaydi. Sizda esa bunday ruxsat yo'q yoki hech bo'lmaganda uni ko'rsatmadingiz.»

paras.en: K. had half sat up, smoothed his hair, looked up at the people from below and said: 'What village have I strayed into? Is there a castle here, then?'
paras.uz: K. yarim ko'tarilib, sochlarini tuzatdi, odamlarga pastdan qarab dedi: «Qaysi qishloqqa adashib keldim? Bu yerda qasr bormi o'zi?»

paras.en: 'There certainly is,' said the young man slowly, while here and there someone shook his head over K., 'the Castle of the Count Westwest.'
paras.uz: — Albatta, — dedi yigit sekin, bu yer-u u yerda kimdir K.ga qarab boshini chayqarkan, — janob graf Vestvestning Qasri.

paras.en: 'And one needs a permit to stay the night?' asked K., as though he wanted to make sure he had not dreamed what he had just been told.
paras.uz: — Tunash uchun ruxsat kerakmi? — so'radi K., go'yo hozirgina aytilgan gaplarni tushida ko'rmaganiga ishonch hosil qilmoqchidek.

paras.en: 'One needs a permit,' was the answer, and there was great mockery of K. in it when the young man stretched out his arm and asked the landlord and the guests: 'Or perhaps one doesn't need a permit?'
paras.uz: — Ruxsat kerak, — degan javob bo'ldi va yigit qo'lini cho'zib, mehmonxona egasi va mehmonlardan: «Yoki ruxsat kerak emasmi?» deb so'raganda, bu javobda K. ustidan katta masxara bor edi.

paras.en: 'Then I shall have to go and get a permit,' said K., yawning, and pushed the blanket off as if he meant to get up.
paras.uz: — Unda ruxsat olishga borishim kerak bo'ladi, — dedi K. esnab va go'yo turmoqchidek ko'rpani o'zidan surdi.

paras.en: 'From whom, may I ask?' said the young man.
paras.uz: — Kimdan, ayting-chi? — so'radi yigit.

paras.en: 'From the Count,' said K., 'there's nothing else for it.'
paras.uz: — Janob grafdan, — dedi K., — boshqa iloji yo'q.

paras.en: 'Get permission from the Count now, at midnight?' cried the young man, and took a step back.
paras.uz: — Hozir, yarim tunda janob grafdan ruxsat olishmi? — deb qichqirdi yigit va bir qadam orqaga chekindi.

paras.en: 'Is that not possible?' asked K. calmly. 'Then why did you wake me?'
paras.uz: — Mumkin emasmi? — so'radi K. xotirjam. — Unda meni nega uyg'otdingiz?

paras.en: At this the young man lost his temper. 'The manners of a tramp!' he cried. 'I demand respect for the Count's authority! I woke you in order to inform you that you must leave the Count's territory at once.'
paras.uz: Shunda yigitning jahli chiqib ketdi. «Daydining odatlari! — qichqirdi u. — Graflik hokimiyatiga hurmat talab qilaman! Sizni graflik hududini darhol tark etishingiz kerakligini ma'lum qilish uchun uyg'otdim.»

paras.en: 'Enough of this comedy,' said K. in a strikingly quiet voice, lay down and drew the blanket over himself. 'You are going a little too far, young man, and I shall come back to your behaviour tomorrow. The landlord and the gentlemen over there are witnesses, so far as I need witnesses at all. For the rest, let me tell you that I am the land surveyor whom the Count has sent for. My assistants with the instruments will follow tomorrow by cart. I did not want to miss the walk through the snow, but unfortunately I lost my way a few times and so arrived only this late. That it was now too late to report at the Castle I knew perfectly well myself, even before your lecture. That is why I made do with this bed for the night, which you have had the — to put it mildly — discourtesy to disturb. That concludes my explanation. Good night, gentlemen.' And K. turned over towards the stove.
paras.uz: — Bu komediya yetar, — dedi K. g'alati darajada past ovozda, yotib, ko'rpani ustiga tortdi. — Yigit, siz biroz haddingizdan oshyapsiz, ertaga xatti-harakatingizga qaytaman. Mehmonxona egasi va anavi janoblar guvoh, umuman guvoh kerak bo'lsa. Boshqa tomondan, bilib qo'yingki, men graf chaqirtirgan yer o'lchovchiman. Yordamchilarim asboblar bilan ertaga arava bilan yetib kelishadi. Men qor bo'ylab piyoda yurishni qo'ldan boy bermoqchi emas edim, lekin afsuski, bir necha marta yo'ldan adashdim va shuning uchun bunchalik kech keldim. Qasrga kelganimni bildirish uchun endi kech ekanini sizning nasihatingizdan oldin ham o'zim yaxshi bilardim. Shuning uchun mana shu tunash joyiga qanoat qildim, siz esa uni buzishga — yumshoqroq aytganda — qo'pollik qildingiz. Mening izohlarim shu bilan tugadi. Xayrli tun, janoblar. — Va K. pechka tomonga o'girildi.

paras.en: 'Land surveyor?' he heard someone ask hesitantly behind his back, and then there was a general silence. But the young man soon collected himself and said to the landlord, in a tone muted enough to pass for consideration of K.'s sleep and loud enough for him to understand: 'I shall enquire by telephone.' What, a telephone in this village inn as well? They were excellently equipped. In detail this surprised K., though on the whole he had expected it. It turned out that the telephone was fixed almost above his head; in his sleepiness he had overlooked it. If the young man now had to telephone, he could not, however much he wished, spare K.'s sleep; the only question was whether K. should let him telephone, and he decided to allow it. But then of course there was no sense in playing the sleeper, and so he turned onto his back again. He saw the peasants shyly drawing together and conferring; the arrival of a land surveyor was no small matter. The kitchen door had opened, and there, filling the doorway, stood the massive figure of the landlady; the landlord approached her on tiptoe to make his report. And now the telephone conversation began. The steward was asleep, but an under-steward, one of the under-stewards, a Herr Fritz, was there.
paras.uz: «Yer o'lchovchi?» — degan ikkilangan savolni orqasida eshitdi u, keyin umumiy sukut cho'kdi. Lekin yigit tez o'zini qo'lga oldi va mehmonxona egasiga K.ning uyqusini hurmat qilishdek ko'rinadigan darajada past, lekin unga eshitiladigan darajada baland ovozda dedi: «Telefon orqali so'rayman.» Nima, bu qishloq mehmonxonasida telefon ham bormi? Ajoyib jihozlangan ekan. Tafsilotlarda bu K.ni hayratga soldi, umuman olganda esa u buni kutgan edi. Telefon deyarli uning boshi ustida o'rnatilgani ma'lum bo'ldi; uyqusirab uni payqamagan edi. Agar yigit endi telefon qilishi kerak bo'lsa, u har qancha istasa ham K.ning uyqusini ayay olmasdi; gap faqat K. unga telefon qilishga yo'l qo'yishi kerakmi, shunda edi, va u yo'l qo'yishga qaror qildi. Lekin unda, albatta, uxlayotgandek ko'rinishning ma'nosi yo'q edi, shuning uchun u yana chalqancha yotdi. U dehqonlar tortinib bir-biriga yaqinlashib, maslahatlashayotganini ko'rdi; yer o'lchovchining kelishi arzimas narsa emas edi. Oshxona eshigi ochilgan edi, eshik o'rnini to'ldirib, mehmonxona bekasining ulkan qomati turardi; mehmonxona egasi unga xabar berish uchun oyoq uchida yaqinlashdi. Va endi telefon suhbati boshlandi. Kastelyan uxlayotgan edi, lekin kastelyan o'rinbosari, o'rinbosarlardan biri, qandaydir janob Frits bor ekan.

paras.en: The young man, who introduced himself as Schwarzer, told how he had found K.: a man in his thirties, rather ragged, sleeping peacefully on a straw sack with a tiny rucksack for a pillow and a knotted stick within reach. Naturally he had seemed suspicious, and since the landlord had evidently neglected his duty, it had been his, Schwarzer's, duty to get to the bottom of the matter. K. had taken very ungraciously the waking, the questioning and the dutiful threat of expulsion from the county — perhaps with reason, as it finally turned out, since he claimed to be a land surveyor engaged by the Count. Of course it was at least a formal duty to check this claim, and Schwarzer therefore asked Herr Fritz to enquire at the Central Office whether a land surveyor of this sort was really expected, and to telephone the answer at once.
paras.uz: O'zini Shvartser deb tanishtirgan yigit K.ni qanday topganini aytib berdi: o'ttiz yoshlardagi, ancha jul-jul kiyingan, somon to'shakda tinch uxlab yotgan, boshi ostida kichkina ryukzak, qo'l yetadigan joyda tugunli hassa turgan odam. Tabiiyki, u unga shubhali ko'rindi, mehmonxona egasi esa o'z burchini e'tiborsiz qoldirgani aniq bo'lgani uchun, ishning tagiga yetish uning, Shvartserning burchi edi. Uyg'otilishni, so'roqni, graflikdan haydash haqidagi burch yuzasidan qilingan tahdidni K. juda norozilik bilan qabul qildi — oxir-oqibat ma'lum bo'lganidek, ehtimol haqli ravishda, chunki u o'zini janob graf chaqirgan yer o'lchovchi deb da'vo qilmoqda. Albatta, bu da'voni tekshirish hech bo'lmaganda rasmiy burch edi, shuning uchun Shvartser janob Fritsdan Markaziy idoradan bunday yer o'lchovchi haqiqatan ham kutilayotganmi, deb so'rab, javobni darhol telefon qilishini iltimos qildi.

paras.en: Then it was quiet; Fritz was making enquiries over there and here they waited for the answer. K. stayed as he was, did not even turn round, seemed not at all curious, and stared in front of him. Schwarzer's report, with its mixture of malice and caution, gave him an idea of the somewhat diplomatic training that even little people like Schwarzer easily commanded at the Castle. And they did not lack diligence there either: the Central Office had a night service. And it evidently answered very quickly, for already Fritz was ringing. His report, however, seemed very short, for Schwarzer at once flung down the receiver in a rage. 'I said so!' he shouted. 'Not a trace of a land surveyor — a common, lying tramp, and probably something worse.' For a moment K. thought that all of them, Schwarzer, peasants, landlord and landlady, would throw themselves on him. To dodge at least the first onslaught he crawled right under the blanket. Then the telephone rang again, and, as it seemed to K., especially loudly. Slowly he put his head out again. Although it was unlikely that it concerned K. again, everyone stopped short, and Schwarzer went back to the apparatus. There he listened to a longer explanation and then said quietly: 'A mistake, then? That is very awkward for me. The head of the office telephoned himself? Strange, strange. How am I to explain it to the land surveyor?'
paras.uz: Keyin jimlik cho'kdi; Frits u yoqda surishtirar, bu yerda esa javobni kutishardi. K. avvalgidek qoldi, hatto o'girilmadi, umuman qiziqmayotgandek, oldiga tikilib yotdi. Shvartserning g'araz va ehtiyotkorlik aralash hikoyasi unga Qasrda hatto Shvartser kabi kichik odamlar ham osongina ega bo'lgan o'ziga xos diplomatik tarbiya haqida tasavvur berdi. U yerda tirishqoqlik ham yetishmasdi; Markaziy idorada tungi navbatchilik bor edi. Va u, aftidan, juda tez javob berdi, chunki Frits allaqachon qo'ng'iroq qilayotgan edi. Lekin bu xabar juda qisqa bo'lsa kerak, chunki Shvartser darhol g'azab bilan go'shakni tashladi. «Aytgandim-ku! — qichqirdi u. — Yer o'lchovchining izi ham yo'q, oddiy, yolg'onchi daydi, ehtimol undan ham yomonrog'i.» Bir lahza K. hammasi — Shvartser, dehqonlar, mehmonxona egasi va bekasi — unga tashlanadi, deb o'yladi. Hech bo'lmaganda birinchi hujumdan qochish uchun u butunlay ko'rpa ostiga sho'ng'idi. Shunda telefon yana jiringladi va, K.ga tuyulishicha, ayniqsa qattiq. U boshini sekin yana chiqardi. Bu yana K.ga tegishli bo'lishi ehtimoldan uzoq bo'lsa ham, hamma to'xtab qoldi va Shvartser apparatga qaytdi. U yerda uzunroq izohni tinglab, keyin past ovozda dedi: «Demak, xato ekanmi? Bu men uchun juda noqulay. Idora boshlig'ining o'zi telefon qildimi? G'alati, g'alati. Janob yer o'lchovchiga buni qanday tushuntiraman?»

paras.en: K. pricked up his ears. So the Castle had appointed him land surveyor. On the one hand this was unfavourable for him, for it showed that the Castle knew everything necessary about him, had weighed up the balance of forces and was taking up the struggle with a smile. On the other hand it was also favourable, for in his opinion it proved that they underestimated him and that he would have more freedom than he could have hoped for at the outset. And if they thought that by acknowledging his surveyorship in this way — intellectually superior, no doubt — they could keep him permanently in fear, they were mistaken; it gave him a slight shiver, but that was all.
paras.uz: K. quloq soldi. Demak, Qasr uni yer o'lchovchi etib tayinlagan ekan. Bu bir tomondan uning uchun noqulay edi, chunki bu Qasrda u haqida barcha kerakli narsalarni bilishlarini, kuchlar nisbatini o'lchab chiqqanlarini va kurashni jilmayib qabul qilganlarini ko'rsatardi. Ikkinchi tomondan esa bu qulay ham edi, chunki bu, uning fikricha, uni past baholashlarini va u boshidan umid qilishi mumkin bo'lganidan ko'ra ko'proq erkinlikka ega bo'lishini isbotlardi. Va agar uning yer o'lchovchiligini bunday — aqlan, albatta, ustun turuvchi — tan olish orqali uni doimo qo'rquvda ushlab turish mumkin deb o'ylashsa, adashishardi; bu uni biroz seskantirdi, lekin hammasi shu edi.

paras.en: K. waved away Schwarzer, who was approaching timidly; he refused to move into the landlord's room, as they urged him to, accepted only a nightcap from the landlord and from the landlady a washbasin with soap and a towel, and did not even have to ask for the room to be cleared, for everyone crowded out with averted faces so as not to be recognized by him the next day. The lamp was put out and at last he had peace. He slept deeply until morning, disturbed only fleetingly, once or twice, by rats scurrying past.
paras.uz: Tortinchoqlik bilan yaqinlashayotgan Shvartserga K. qo'l siltab qo'ydi; uni undashganidek mehmonxona egasining xonasiga ko'chishdan bosh tortdi, faqat mehmonxona egasidan uyqu oldidan ichimlik, bekasidan esa sovun va sochiqli tog'ora oldi va zalni bo'shatishni so'rashga ham hojat qolmadi, chunki hamma ertaga u tomonidan tanib qolinmaslik uchun yuzlarini o'girib, tashqariga yopirildi. Chiroq o'chirildi va u nihoyat tinchlik topdi. U tonggacha qattiq uxladi, faqat bir-ikki marta yugurib o'tgan kalamushlar uni bir zum bezovta qildi.

paras.en: After breakfast — which, like all K.'s board, was to be paid for by the Castle, according to the landlord — he wanted to go straight into the village. But since the landlord, with whom he had so far exchanged only what was necessary because of his behaviour the night before, kept circling round him with a silent plea, he took pity on him and let him sit down with him for a little while.
paras.uz: Nonushtadan keyin — mehmonxona egasining aytishicha, K.ning butun ovqati kabi bu ham Qasr tomonidan to'lanishi kerak edi — u darhol qishloqqa chiqmoqchi bo'ldi. Lekin kechagi xatti-harakatini eslab, hozircha faqat eng zarur gaplarni gaplashgan mehmonxona egasi indamay iltijo bilan uning atrofida aylanib yurgani uchun, K. unga rahmi kelib, uni bir oz yoniga o'tqazdi.

paras.en: 'I don't know the Count yet,' said K. 'He is said to pay well for good work — is that true? When one travels as far from wife and child as I have, one wants to take something home.'
paras.uz: — Men grafni hali tanimayman, — dedi K. — Aytishlaricha, u yaxshi ish uchun yaxshi haq to'larkan, rostmi? Men kabi xotini va bolasidan shunchalik uzoqqa yo'l olgan odam uyga biror narsa olib qaytishni istaydi-da.

paras.en: 'In that respect the gentleman need have no worries; one hears no complaints about poor pay.' — 'Well,' said K., 'I'm not one of the timid sort and I can tell even a count what I think, but of course it is far better to get on with the gentlemen in peace.'
paras.uz: — Bu jihatdan janob tashvishlanmasa ham bo'ladi, yomon haq to'lashdan hech kim nolimaydi. — Xo'sh, — dedi K., — men tortinchoqlardan emasman, hatto grafga ham fikrimni ayta olaman, lekin janoblar bilan tinch-totuv kelishib olish, albatta, ancha yaxshi.

paras.en: The landlord sat opposite K. on the edge of the window seat — he did not dare sit more comfortably — and all the while looked at K. with large, brown, anxious eyes. At first he had pressed himself on K., and now it seemed he would most like to run away. Was he afraid of being questioned about the Count? Did he fear the unreliability of the 'gentleman' he took K. to be? K. had to distract him. He looked at the clock and said: 'My assistants will be here soon now; will you be able to put them up?'
paras.uz: Mehmonxona egasi K.ning ro'parasida deraza tokchasining chetida o'tirardi — qulayroq o'tirishga jur'at etmasdi — va butun vaqt davomida K.ga katta, jigarrang, xavotirli ko'zlari bilan qarab turardi. Avvaliga u K.ga yopishib olgan edi, endi esa eng ko'p qochib ketishni istayotgandek tuyulardi. Undan graf haqida so'rab qolishlaridan qo'rqarmidi? U K.ni deb bilgan «janob»ning ishonchsizligidan qo'rqarmidi? K. uni chalg'itishi kerak edi. U soatga qarab dedi: «Endi tez orada yordamchilarim kelishadi, ularni shu yerga joylashtira olasanmi?»

paras.en: 'Certainly, sir,' he said, 'but won't they live with you up at the Castle?'
paras.uz: — Albatta, taqsir, — dedi u, — lekin ular sen bilan Qasrda yashamaydilarmi?

paras.en: Did he give up guests so easily and so gladly — and K. in particular, whom he was so determined to send off to the Castle?
paras.uz: Nahotki u mehmonlardan, ayniqsa uni albatta Qasrga jo'natmoqchi bo'lgan K.dan shunchalik oson va bajonidil voz kechsa?

paras.en: 'That is not certain yet,' said K. 'First I must find out what sort of work they have for me. If, for instance, I am to work down here, it will be more sensible to live down here too. Besides, I'm afraid that life up at the Castle would not suit me. I always want to be free.'
paras.uz: — Bu hali aniq emas, — dedi K., — avval men uchun qanday ish borligini bilishim kerak. Masalan, agar bu yerda, pastda ishlashim kerak bo'lsa, pastda yashash ham oqilonaroq bo'ladi. Buning ustiga, yuqorida, Qasrdagi hayot menga yoqmasa kerak, deb qo'rqaman. Men doim erkin bo'lishni istayman.

paras.en: 'You don't know the Castle,' said the landlord quietly.
paras.uz: — Sen Qasrni bilmaysan, — dedi mehmonxona egasi sekin.

paras.en: 'True,' said K., 'one shouldn't judge too early. For the time being all I know of the Castle is that they know how to pick the right land surveyor there. Perhaps it has other merits as well.' And he stood up, to rid himself of the landlord, who was nervously biting his lips. This man's confidence was not easily won.
paras.uz: — To'g'ri, — dedi K., — shoshilib hukm chiqarmaslik kerak. Hozircha men Qasr haqida faqat bir narsani bilaman: u yerda to'g'ri yer o'lchovchini tanlashni bilishadi. Balki uning boshqa afzalliklari ham bordir. — Va u xavotir bilan labini tishlayotgan mehmonxona egasidan qutulish uchun o'rnidan turdi. Bu odamning ishonchini qozonish oson emas edi.

paras.en: On his way out K. noticed on the wall a dark portrait in a dark frame. He had seen it already from his bed, but at that distance had not made out the details and had thought the actual picture had been taken out of the frame and only a black backing was visible. But it was a picture after all, as now appeared: the head and shoulders of a man of about fifty. He held his head so low on his chest that one could hardly see his eyes; what seemed to press it down was the high, heavy forehead and the strong, hooked nose. His full beard, squashed in at the chin by the position of his head, jutted out further down. His left hand lay spread in his thick hair but could no longer lift the head. 'Who is that?' asked K. 'The Count?' K. stood in front of the picture and did not even look round at the landlord. 'No,' said the landlord, 'the steward.' — 'They have a handsome steward at the Castle, that's true,' said K. 'A pity he has such a badly brought-up son.' — 'No,' said the landlord, drew K. down a little towards him and whispered in his ear: 'Schwarzer exaggerated yesterday. His father is only an under-steward, and one of the lowest at that.' At that moment the landlord seemed to K. like a child. 'The scoundrel!' said K., laughing, but the landlord did not laugh with him; instead he said: 'His father is powerful too.' — 'Go on!' said K.
paras.uz: Chiqib ketayotib K. devorda qora ramkadagi qorong'i portretni payqadi. Uni to'shagidan ham ko'rgan edi, lekin uzoqdan tafsilotlarini ajrata olmagan va asl rasm ramkadan olib qo'yilgan, faqat qora orqa taxta ko'rinyapti, deb o'ylagan edi. Lekin endi ma'lum bo'ldiki, bu baribir rasm ekan — ellik yoshlardagi erkakning ko'kragigacha bo'lgan tasviri. U boshini ko'kragiga shunchalik past egib turardiki, ko'zlari deyarli ko'rinmasdi; boshni pastga bosib turgandek tuyulgan narsa — baland, og'ir peshona va kuchli, pastga egilgan burun edi. Boshning holati tufayli iyagida bosilib qolgan to'la soqoli pastroqda turtib chiqqan edi. Chap qo'li qalin sochlari orasida yoyilib yotardi, lekin boshni endi ko'tara olmasdi. «Bu kim? — so'radi K. — Grafmi?» K. rasm oldida turar va mehmonxona egasiga o'girilib ham qaramasdi. «Yo'q, — dedi mehmonxona egasi, — kastelyan.» — «Qasrda chiroyli kastelyan bor ekan, to'g'ri, — dedi K., — afsuski, uning shunday tarbiyasiz o'g'li bor.» — «Yo'q, — dedi mehmonxona egasi va K.ni o'ziga biroz egib, qulog'iga pichirladi: — Shvartser kecha mubolag'a qildi, otasi faqat kastelyan o'rinbosari, hatto eng quyilaridan biri.» Shu lahzada mehmonxona egasi K.ga boladek ko'rindi. «Yaramas!» — dedi K. kulib, lekin mehmonxona egasi u bilan birga kulmadi, balki: «Uning otasi ham qudratli», dedi. — «Qo'ysangchi!» — dedi K.

paras.en: 'You think everyone is powerful. Me too, perhaps?' — 'You,' he said shyly but seriously, 'I do not think powerful.' — 'So you are a good observer after all,' said K. 'For, between ourselves, I really am not powerful. And consequently I probably have no less respect for the powerful than you do, only I am not as honest as you and don't always like to admit it.' And K. patted the landlord lightly on the cheek, to comfort him and win him over. Now he did smile a little. He really was a boy, with his soft, almost beardless face. How had he come by his broad, elderly wife, whom one could see next door through a hatch, bustling about the kitchen with her elbows stuck far out? But K. did not want to press him any further now and chase away the smile he had finally coaxed out of him. So he merely signed to him to open the door, and stepped out into the beautiful winter morning.
paras.uz: — Sen hammani qudratli deb bilasan. Balki meni ham? — Seni, — dedi u tortinib, lekin jiddiy, — qudratli deb bilmayman. — Demak, sen baribir yaxshi kuzatar ekansan, — dedi K., — chunki, oramizda qolsin, men haqiqatan ham qudratli emasman. Shuning uchun, ehtimol, qudratlilarga hurmatim sendan kam emas, faqat men sendek samimiy emasman va buni doim tan olishni istamayman. — Va K. uni yupatish va o'ziga moyil qilish uchun mehmonxona egasining yuziga yengil shapatiladi. Endi u baribir biroz jilmaydi. U yumshoq, deyarli soqolsiz yuzi bilan haqiqatan bola edi. Qanday qilib u yon tomondagi tuynuk orqali oshxonada tirsaklarini tanasidan uzoq kerib, ivirsib yurganini ko'rish mumkin bo'lgan keng gavdali, yoshi o'tgan xotiniga ega bo'lib qolgan? Lekin K. endi unga boshqa yopishmoqchi emas, nihoyat yuzaga chiqargan jilmayishni haydab yubormoqchi emas edi. Shuning uchun unga faqat eshikni ochishga ishora qildi va go'zal qishki tongga chiqdi.

paras.en: Now he saw the Castle up above, clearly outlined in the clear air and made even clearer by the snow, which lay everywhere in a thin layer and traced every shape. Incidentally, there seemed to be much less snow up on the hill than here in the village, where K. made his way forward no less laboriously than yesterday on the high road. Here the snow reached up to the cottage windows and lay heavy again at once on the low roofs, but up on the hill everything rose free and light — or so it seemed from here.
paras.uz: Endi u tepada Qasrni tiniq havoda aniq ko'rdi, hamma joyda yupqa qatlam bo'lib yotgan va barcha shakllarni takrorlaydigan qor uni yanada aniqroq qilib ko'rsatardi. Aytgancha, tepada, tog'da qor bu yerdagi qishloqdagidan ancha kamdek tuyulardi; bu yerda esa K. kecha katta yo'lda bo'lganidan kam qiyinchilik bilan oldinga siljimasdi. Bu yerda qor kulbalarning derazalarigacha yetar va darhol past tomlarga og'ir bosib yotardi, tepada, tog'da esa hamma narsa erkin va yengil ko'tarilib turardi — hech bo'lmaganda bu yerdan shunday ko'rinardi.

paras.en: On the whole the Castle, as it showed itself from a distance here, met K.'s expectations. It was neither an old knight's castle nor a showy new building, but a sprawling complex made up of a few two-storey buildings and a great many low ones standing close together; had one not known it was a castle, one might have taken it for a little town. K. saw only one tower; whether it belonged to a dwelling or to a church could not be made out. Flocks of crows circled round it. With his eyes fixed on the Castle K. walked on; nothing else concerned him. But as he came closer the Castle disappointed him: it was after all only a rather wretched little town, pieced together from village houses, distinguished only by the fact that perhaps everything was built of stone; but the paint had long since flaked off and the stone seemed to be crumbling. Fleetingly K. remembered his own home town; it was hardly inferior to this so-called castle. Had K. come only for the sightseeing, the long journey would have been wasted, and he would have done more sensibly to visit his old home again, where he had not been for so long. And in his mind he compared the church tower at home with the tower up there.
paras.uz: Umuman olganda, bu yerdan, uzoqdan ko'ringan Qasr K.ning kutganlariga mos kelardi. U na eski ritsar qal'asi, na yangi dabdabali bino edi, balki bir necha ikki qavatli va ko'plab bir-biriga zich turgan past binolardan iborat keng majmua edi; agar uning qasr ekanini bilmaganingizda, uni kichik shaharcha deb o'ylashingiz mumkin edi. K. faqat bitta minorani ko'rdi; u turar joy binosigami yoki cherkovgami tegishli ekanini ajratib bo'lmasdi. Qarg'alar galasi uning atrofida aylanardi. Ko'zlarini Qasrga tikib, K. yurishda davom etdi, boshqa hech narsa uni qiziqtirmasdi. Lekin yaqinlashgan sari Qasr uning ko'nglini qoldirdi: bu baribir qishloq uylaridan yig'ib qo'yilgan ancha bechora shaharcha edi, faqat, ehtimol, hammasi toshdan qurilgani bilan ajralib turardi; lekin bo'yog'i allaqachon ko'chib tushgan, toshi esa uvalanayotgandek edi. K. bir zum o'z ona shaharchasini esladi; u bu qasr deb atalmishdan deyarli qolishmasdi. Agar K. faqat tomosha qilish uchun kelgan bo'lsa, uzoq yo'l bekorga ketgan bo'lardi va u uzoq vaqtdan beri bormagan eski vataniga yana bir bor borsa, oqilonaroq ish qilgan bo'lardi. Va u xayolan ona shahridagi cherkov minorasini tepadagi minora bilan solishtirdi.

paras.en: That tower — firm, tapering straight upward without hesitation, broad-roofed, finished off with red tiles: an earthly building — what else can we build? — but with a higher aim than the low huddle of houses, and with a clearer expression than the dull working day has. The tower up here — the only one visible — the tower of a dwelling house, as it now turned out, perhaps of the main castle, was a monotonous round building, partly and mercifully hidden by ivy, with small windows that now flashed in the sun — there was something mad about it — and a balcony-like top whose battlements jagged into the blue sky, uncertain, irregular, brittle, as if drawn by a frightened or careless child's hand. It was as though some melancholy occupant of the house, who by rights ought to have kept himself locked away in its remotest room, had broken through the roof and stood up to show himself to the world.
paras.uz: O'sha minora qat'iy, ikkilanmasdan to'g'ri yuqoriga ingichkalashib borar, keng tomli, qizil cherepitsa bilan tugallangan edi — yerdagi bino, biz yana nima qura olardik? — lekin past uylar to'dasidan ko'ra yuksakroq maqsadli va xira ish kunidan ko'ra aniqroq ifodali edi. Bu yerdagi, tepadagi minora — yagona ko'rinib turgani — ma'lum bo'lishicha, turar joy binosining, ehtimol, asosiy qasrning minorasi bo'lib, bir xil dumaloq bino edi, qisman pechak bilan rahmdillik bilan yopilgan, hozir quyoshda chaqnayotgan kichik derazalari bor edi — bunda qandaydir telbalik bor edi — va tepasi ayvonsimon bo'lib, uning devor tishlari ishonchsiz, notekis, mo'rt — go'yo qo'rqqan yoki beparvo bola qo'li bilan chizilgandek — moviy osmonga tishli bo'lib kirib turardi. Go'yo adolat yuzasidan uyning eng chekka xonasiga qamalib o'tirishi kerak bo'lgan qandaydir g'amgin uy egasi tomni yorib chiqib, o'zini dunyoga ko'rsatish uchun qad rostlagandek edi.

paras.en: Again K. stood still, as if standing still gave him more power of judgement. But he was disturbed. Behind the village church, by which he had stopped — it was really only a chapel, enlarged like a barn so as to hold the congregation — was the school. A long, low building, oddly combining the character of something makeshift and something very old, it lay behind a fenced garden that was now a field of snow. Just then the children were coming out with the teacher. They surrounded him in a dense crowd, every eye fixed on him, chattering ceaselessly from all sides; K. could not follow their rapid talk at all. The teacher, a small, young, narrow-shouldered man who held himself very upright, though without becoming ridiculous, had already fixed K. with his eyes from a distance — though apart from his group, K. was the only human being far and wide. K., as the stranger, greeted him first, especially as he was such a commanding little man. 'Good morning, teacher,' he said. At one stroke the children fell silent; this sudden stillness as a preparation for his words probably pleased the teacher. 'You are looking at the Castle?' he asked, more gently than K. had expected, but in a tone as if he did not approve of what K. was doing. 'Yes,' said K., 'I'm a stranger here, I only arrived last night.' — 'You don't like the Castle?' the teacher asked quickly.
paras.uz: K. yana to'xtadi, go'yo to'xtab turganda hukm chiqarish kuchi ko'proq bo'ladigandek. Lekin uni bezovta qilishdi. U to'xtagan qishloq cherkovining orqasida — aslida bu jamoani sig'dirish uchun omborxonadek kengaytirilgan kichik ibodatxona edi — maktab bor edi. Vaqtinchalik va juda eski xususiyatlarni g'alati birlashtirgan past, uzun bino hozir qor maydoniga aylangan panjarali bog' orqasida turardi. Aynan shu payt bolalar o'qituvchi bilan chiqib kelishayotgan edi. Ular o'qituvchini zich to'da bo'lib o'rab olishgan, hammaning ko'zi unda, har tomondan tinimsiz vaqillashardi; K. ularning tez gaplarini umuman tushunmasdi. O'qituvchi — yosh, kichkina, yelkalari tor, lekin kulgili bo'lmagan holda juda tik turadigan odam — K.ni uzoqdan ko'zdan qo'ymagan edi, garchi uning guruhidan tashqari atrofda K.dan boshqa hech kim yo'q edi. K. begona sifatida, ayniqsa shunday buyruqbozona kichkina odamga, birinchi bo'lib salom berdi. «Xayrli kun, janob o'qituvchi», dedi u. Bolalar birdaniga jim bo'lib qolishdi; uning so'zlariga tayyorgarlik sifatidagi bu to'satdan sukunat o'qituvchiga yoqqan bo'lsa kerak. «Qasrni tomosha qilyapsizmi?» — so'radi u K. kutganidan muloyimroq, lekin K. qilayotgan ishni ma'qullamayotgandek ohangda. «Ha, — dedi K., — men bu yerda begonaman, kecha kechqurundan beri qishloqdaman.» — «Qasr sizga yoqmayaptimi?» — tez so'radi o'qituvchi.

paras.en: 'What?' asked K. in return, a little taken aback, and repeated the question in a milder form: 'Whether I like the Castle? Why do you assume that I don't?' — 'No stranger likes it,' said the teacher. To avoid saying anything unwelcome here, K. changed the subject and asked: 'You know the Count, I suppose?' — 'No,' said the teacher and made to turn away. But K. would not give up and asked again: 'What? You don't know the Count?' — 'How should I know him?' said the teacher quietly, and added aloud in French: 'Please consider the presence of innocent children.' K. took this as a right to ask: 'Might I visit you some time, teacher? I shall be staying here for quite a while and already feel a little lost; I don't belong among the peasants, and probably not at the Castle either.' — 'There is no great difference between the peasants and the Castle,' said the teacher. 'That may be,' said K., 'it doesn't change my position. Might I visit you some time?' — 'I live in Swan Street, at the butcher's.' This was more the giving of an address than an invitation, but K. still said: 'Good, I'll come.' The teacher nodded and moved off with his crowd of children, who at once started shouting again. They soon disappeared down a steep little lane.
paras.uz: — Nima? — deb qayta so'radi K. biroz hayron bo'lib va savolni yumshoqroq shaklda takrorladi: — Qasr menga yoqadimi? Nega u menga yoqmaydi, deb taxmin qilyapsiz? — Hech bir begonaga yoqmaydi, — dedi o'qituvchi. Bu yerda biror noxush gap aytmaslik uchun K. suhbatni burdi va so'radi: — Siz grafni taniysizmi? — Yo'q, — dedi o'qituvchi va burilib ketmoqchi bo'ldi. Lekin K. bo'sh kelmadi va yana so'radi: — Nima? Grafni tanimaysizmi? — Qanday qilib uni tanishim mumkin? — dedi o'qituvchi sekin va ovozini ko'tarib fransuzcha qo'shib qo'ydi: — Begunoh bolalarning huzurini hisobga oling. — K. bundan so'rash huquqini oldi: — Janob o'qituvchi, sizni bir kun ziyorat qilsam bo'ladimi? Men bu yerda uzoqroq qolaman va hozirdanoq o'zimni biroz tashlab qo'yilgandek his qilyapman; men dehqonlarga tegishli emasman, Qasrga ham, ehtimol, tegishli emasman. — Dehqonlar bilan Qasr o'rtasida katta farq yo'q, — dedi o'qituvchi. — Bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi K., — bu mening ahvolimni o'zgartirmaydi. Sizni bir kun ziyorat qilsam bo'ladimi? — Men Oqqush ko'chasida, qassobnikida yashayman. — Bu taklifdan ko'ra ko'proq manzil aytish edi, shunga qaramay K. dedi: — Yaxshi, kelaman. — O'qituvchi bosh irg'adi va darhol yana qichqira boshlagan bolalar to'dasi bilan yo'lida davom etdi. Ular tez orada tik pastlab ketgan tor ko'chada g'oyib bo'lishdi.

paras.en: K., though, was distracted and annoyed by the conversation. For the first time since he had come he felt real tiredness. The long way here had at first not seemed to tax him at all — how he had wandered through the days, calmly, step by step! But now the consequences of the excessive strain were showing after all, at the wrong moment, of course. He was irresistibly drawn to seek new acquaintances, but every new acquaintance made the tiredness worse. If, in his present state, he forced himself to extend his walk at least as far as the entrance to the Castle, that would be more than enough.
paras.uz: K. esa parishon, suhbatdan achchiqlangan edi. Kelganidan beri birinchi marta u haqiqiy charchoqni his qildi. Bu yerga uzoq yo'l avvaliga uni umuman charchatmagandek tuyulgan edi — u kunlar davomida qanday xotirjam, qadam-baqadam yurgan edi! Endi esa haddan tashqari zo'riqishning oqibatlari, albatta, noo'rin paytda, baribir namoyon bo'lmoqda edi. Uni yangi tanishlar izlashga qarshilik qilib bo'lmas tarzda tortardi, lekin har bir yangi tanishuv charchoqni kuchaytirardi. Agar u bugungi holatida o'zini hech bo'lmaganda Qasr darvozasigacha sayr qilishga majbur qilsa, bu yetarlidan ham ortiq bo'lardi.

paras.en: So he walked on, but it was a long way. For the street, the main street of the village, did not lead to the Castle hill; it only led close to it, and then, as if on purpose, it turned aside, and though it did not move away from the Castle, it came no nearer to it either. K. kept expecting that now at last the street must turn towards the Castle, and only because he expected it did he go on; evidently because of his tiredness he hesitated to leave the street, and he was also astonished at the length of the village, which had no end — again and again the little houses and the frozen window panes and snow and no people — at last he tore himself away from this clinging street; a narrow lane took him in, the snow even deeper, pulling out his sinking feet was heavy work, he broke into a sweat, suddenly he stood still and could go no further.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib u yana oldinga yurdi, lekin yo'l uzoq edi. Chunki ko'cha, qishloqning asosiy ko'chasi Qasr tepaligiga olib bormasdi; u faqat unga yaqin olib borardi, keyin esa go'yo ataylab burilib ketardi va Qasrdan uzoqlashmasa-da, unga yaqinlashmasdi ham. K. doim endi nihoyat ko'cha Qasr tomon burilishi kerak, deb kutardi va faqat shuni kutgani uchun yurishda davom etardi; aftidan charchoqdan ko'chani tark etishga ikkilanardi, buning ustiga qishloqning uzunligidan hayratda edi — oxiri yo'q edi, yana va yana kichkina uychalar, muzlagan deraza oynalari, qor va odamsizlik — nihoyat u o'zini tutib turgan bu ko'chadan yulib oldi, uni tor bir ko'cha qabul qildi, qor yanada chuqurroq, botib ketayotgan oyoqlarni tortib chiqarish og'ir mehnat edi, uni ter bosdi, birdan u to'xtadi va boshqa yura olmadi.

paras.en: Well, he was not forsaken; to right and left stood peasants' cottages. He made a snowball and threw it at a window. At once the door opened — the first door to open during his whole walk through the village — and an old peasant in a brown fur jacket, his head tilted to one side, friendly and frail, stood there. 'May I come in to you for a little?' said K. 'I'm very tired.' He did not hear what the old man said at all; gratefully he accepted a board being pushed out towards him, which rescued him from the snow at once, and in a few steps he was standing in the room.
paras.uz: Axir u tashlab qo'yilgan emas edi, o'ngda ham, chapda ham dehqon kulbalari turardi. U qor bo'lagi yasab, uni bir derazaga otdi. Darhol eshik ochildi — butun qishloq yo'li davomida ochilgan birinchi eshik — va jigarrang mo'ynali kalta kamzul kiygan, boshini yon tomonga egib turgan, mehribon va zaif bir keksa dehqon turardi. «Biroz yoningizga kirsam bo'ladimi? — dedi K. — Juda charchadim.» U cholning nima deganini umuman eshitmadi; uni darhol qordan qutqargan, unga qarab surib qo'yilgan taxtani minnatdorlik bilan qabul qildi va bir necha qadamda xonada turardi.

paras.en: A big room in half-darkness. Coming in from outside, one saw nothing at first. K. stumbled against a washtub; a woman's hand held him back. From one corner came a great deal of children's screaming. From another corner smoke came rolling out and turned the half-light into darkness. K. stood as if in clouds. 'He's drunk,' someone said. 'Who are you?' called a domineering voice, and, turning to the old man no doubt: 'Why did you let him in? Can one let in everything that slinks about the lanes?' — 'I am the Count's land surveyor,' said K., trying in this way to justify himself to the still invisible people. 'Oh, it's the land surveyor,' said a woman's voice, and then there followed a complete silence. 'You know me?' asked K. 'Certainly,' said the same voice curtly. That he was known did not seem to recommend him.
paras.uz: Katta, g'ira-shira xona. Tashqaridan kirgan odam avvaliga hech narsani ko'rmasdi. K. kir yuvish tog'orasiga qoqilib ketdi, bir ayol qo'li uni ushlab qoldi. Bir burchakdan ko'p bolalar qichqirig'i kelardi. Boshqa burchakdan tutun yumalab chiqar va yarim yorug'likni zulmatga aylantirardi. K. go'yo bulutlar ichida turardi. «U mast-ku», dedi kimdir. «Kimsiz?» — deb qichqirdi buyruqbozona ovoz va, ehtimol, cholga o'girilib: «Nega uni kiritding? Ko'chalarda sudralib yurgan hamma narsani kiritish mumkinmi?» — «Men graflikning yer o'lchovchisiman», dedi K. va shu tarzda hamon ko'rinmayotganlar oldida o'zini oqlashga urindi. «Ha, bu yer o'lchovchi ekan», dedi ayol ovozi va endi to'liq sukut cho'kdi. «Meni taniysizlarmi?» — so'radi K. «Albatta», dedi o'sha ovoz qisqagina. K.ni tanishlari unga yaxshi tavsiya bo'lmayotgandek edi.

paras.en: At last the smoke cleared a little and K. could slowly find his bearings. It seemed to be a general washing day. Near the door clothes were being washed. But the smoke had come from the other corner, where in a wooden tub — bigger than any K. had ever seen, roughly the size of two beds — two men were bathing in steaming water. But even more surprising, without one quite knowing what was surprising about it, was the right-hand corner. There, from a large opening, the only one in the back wall of the room, pale snow-light came in, probably from the yard, and gave a sheen like silk to the dress of a woman who was lying, almost, tired, deep in the corner in a high armchair. She held a baby at her breast. A few children were playing around her, peasant children, as could be seen, but she did not seem to belong to them; though, of course, illness and tiredness make even peasants refined.
paras.uz: Nihoyat tutun biroz tarqaldi va K. asta-sekin mo'ljal ola boshladi. Umumiy kir yuvish kuni bo'lsa kerak. Eshik yaqinida kir yuvilardi. Lekin tutun boshqa burchakdan kelgan edi, u yerda K. hali hech qachon ko'rmagan kattalikdagi yog'och tog'orada — u taxminan ikki karavot kattaligida edi — bug'lanib turgan suvda ikki erkak cho'milardi. Lekin bundan ham hayratlanarliroq — garchi hayratlanarli narsa aynan nimada ekanini aniq bilmasa ham — o'ng burchak edi. U yerda xonaning orqa devoridagi yagona katta tuynukdan, ehtimol hovlidan, oqish qor yorug'i tushar va burchakning chuqurida baland suyanchiqli kresloda charchab, deyarli yotgan bir ayolning ko'ylagiga ipakdek yaltiroq berardi. U ko'kragida go'dak emizardi. Uning atrofida bir necha bola — ko'rinib turganidek, dehqon bolalari — o'ynardi, lekin u ularga tegishli emasdek tuyulardi; albatta, kasallik va charchoq dehqonlarni ham nozik qilib qo'yadi.

paras.en: 'Sit down!' said one of the men, a full-bearded man who also had a moustache under which he kept his mouth open, panting; comically, he pointed over the rim of the tub to a chest and in doing so splashed K.'s whole face with warm water. On the chest, already dozing, sat the old man who had let K. in. K. was grateful to be allowed to sit down at last. Now nobody bothered about him any more. The woman at the washtub, fair-haired, in the plumpness of youth, sang softly at her work; the men in the bath stamped and turned about; the children wanted to get near them but were driven back again and again by mighty splashes of water that did not spare K. either; the woman in the armchair lay as if lifeless, not even looking down at the child at her breast, but vaguely upwards.
paras.uz: — O'tiringlar! — dedi erkaklardan biri, to'la soqolli, buning ustiga mo'ylovli odam; mo'ylovi ostida og'zini doim ochib, pishillab nafas olardi. U tog'ora chetidan qo'li bilan kulgili tarzda sandiqni ko'rsatdi va bunda K.ning butun yuziga iliq suv sachratdi. Sandiq ustida allaqachon mudrab, K.ni kiritgan chol o'tirardi. K. nihoyat o'tirishga ruxsat berilganidan minnatdor edi. Endi hech kim unga e'tibor bermasdi. Kir tog'orasi yonidagi ayol — sariq sochli, yoshlik to'laligida — ishlayotib sekin qo'shiq aytardi, cho'milayotgan erkaklar depsinar va aylanar, bolalar ularga yaqinlashmoqchi bo'lishar, lekin K.ni ham ayamaydigan kuchli suv sachratishlari bilan qayta-qayta haydalardi; kreslodagi ayol jonsizdek yotardi, hatto ko'kragidagi bolaga ham qaramas, balki noaniq yuqoriga tikilib turardi.

paras.en: K. must have looked at her for a long time, at this beautiful, sad, unchanging picture, but then he must have fallen asleep, for when he started up, called by a loud voice, his head was lying on the shoulder of the old man beside him. The men had finished their bath — the children were now romping about in it, watched by the fair woman — and stood dressed in front of K. It turned out that the shouting, full-bearded one was the lesser of the two. The other, no taller than the bearded one and with a much slighter beard, was a quiet, slow-thinking man of broad build, with a broad face too; he held his head lowered. 'Land surveyor,' he said, 'you can't stay here. Forgive the discourtesy.' — 'I didn't mean to stay,' said K., 'only to rest a little. I have done that, and now I'll go.' — 'You are probably surprised at our lack of hospitality,' said the man, 'but hospitality is not our custom; we have no need of guests.' A little refreshed by his sleep, a little sharper of hearing than before, K. was glad of the frank words. He moved more freely, planted his stick now here, now there, went closer to the woman in the armchair; he was, besides, physically the biggest person in the room.
paras.uz: K. bu o'zgarmas, go'zal, g'amgin manzaraga uzoq qaragan bo'lsa kerak, lekin keyin uxlab qolgan bo'lsa kerak, chunki baland ovoz chaqirganidan cho'chib uyg'onganida, boshi yonidagi cholning yelkasida yotardi. Erkaklar cho'milishni tugatishgan edi — endi tog'orada sariq sochli ayol nazorati ostida bolalar o'ynab yurishardi — va kiyingan holda K.ning oldida turishardi. Ma'lum bo'ldiki, baqiroq, to'la soqolli odam ikkovining arzimasrog'i ekan. Ikkinchisi — to'la soqollidan baland bo'lmagan va ancha siyrak soqolli — sokin, sekin fikrlaydigan, keng gavdali, yuzi ham keng odam edi, boshini egib turardi. «Janob yer o'lchovchi, — dedi u, — bu yerda qola olmaysiz. Qo'polligimizni kechiring.» — «Men qolmoqchi ham emas edim, — dedi K., — faqat biroz dam olmoqchi edim. Dam oldim, endi ketaman.» — «Mehmondo'stligimiz kamligidan hayron bo'layotgandirsiz, — dedi erkak, — lekin mehmondo'stlik bizda odat emas, bizga mehmonlar kerak emas.» Uyqudan biroz tetiklashgan, avvalgidan biroz sezgirroq bo'lgan K. ochiq so'zlardan xursand bo'ldi. U erkinroq harakat qila boshladi, hassasini goh u yerga, goh bu yerga tiradi, kreslodagi ayolga yaqinlashdi; aytgancha, jismonan ham xonadagi eng katta odam u edi.

paras.en: 'Of course,' said K., 'what would you need guests for? But now and then one does need one — me, for example, the land surveyor.' — 'I don't know about that,' said the man slowly. 'If you were sent for, then you are probably needed; that is an exception, I suppose. But we, we little people, keep to the rule; you can't hold that against us.' — 'No, no,' said K., 'I have only to thank you, you and everyone here.' And, unexpectedly for everyone, K. turned round with what was practically a leap and stood before the woman. She looked at K. out of tired blue eyes; a transparent silk kerchief came down to the middle of her forehead; the baby was asleep at her breast. 'Who are you?' asked K. Dismissively — it was unclear whether her contempt was meant for K. or for her own answer — she said: 'A girl from the Castle.'
paras.uz: — Albatta, — dedi K., — sizlarga mehmon nimaga kerak? Lekin ba'zan baribir kimdir kerak bo'ladi, masalan, men — yer o'lchovchi. — Buni bilmayman, — dedi erkak sekin, — agar sizni chaqirishgan bo'lsa, demak, siz kerak bo'lsangiz kerak, bu istisno bo'lsa kerak, lekin biz, kichik odamlar, qoidaga amal qilamiz, buni bizdan ayb ko'rmang. — Yo'q, yo'q, — dedi K., — men sizga faqat minnatdorman, sizga va bu yerdagi hammaga. — Va hamma uchun kutilmaganda K. deyarli bir sakrashda o'girildi va ayolning oldida turdi. Ayol unga charchagan moviy ko'zlari bilan qaradi; shaffof ipak ro'mol peshonasining o'rtasigacha tushib turardi, go'dak ko'kragida uxlardi. «Sen kimsan?» — so'radi K. Mensimay — bu nafrat K.gami yoki o'z javobigami qaratilgani noaniq edi — u dedi: «Qasrdan kelgan bir qiz.»

paras.en: All this had lasted only a moment; already K. had one of the men on his right and one on his left, and, as if there were no other means of making themselves understood, he was pulled to the door in silence but with all their strength. The old man was delighted at something in this and clapped his hands. The washerwoman laughed too, among the children, who had suddenly started making a mad din.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi bir lahza davom etdi xolos; K.ning o'ng va chap tomonida allaqachon erkaklarning biri turardi va, go'yo tushunishishning boshqa vositasi yo'qdek, uni indamay, lekin butun kuchlari bilan eshik tomon sudrashdi. Chol nimagadir xursand bo'lib, qarsak chaldi. Kir yuvuvchi ayol ham birdan telbalardek shovqin ko'targan bolalar orasida kuldi.

paras.en: But K. was soon standing in the lane, the men watching him from the threshold. Snow was falling again; even so, it seemed a little lighter. The bearded man called impatiently: 'Where do you want to go? This way leads to the Castle, this way to the village.' K. did not answer him, but to the other, who despite his superiority seemed the more approachable, he said: 'Who are you? Whom have I to thank for my rest?' — 'I am the master tanner Lasemann,' was the answer, 'but you have nobody to thank.' — 'Good,' said K., 'perhaps we shall meet again.' — 'I don't think so,' said the man. At that moment the bearded man raised his hand and called: 'Good day, Artur! Good day, Jeremias!' K. turned round — so there were people in the lanes of this village after all! From the direction of the Castle came two young men of medium height, both very slim, in tight clothes, and very alike in face as well. Their complexion was a dark brown, against which their pointed beards nonetheless stood out in their particular blackness. Considering the state of the road they walked astonishingly fast, flinging out their slim legs in step. 'What's up with you?' called the bearded man. One could only make oneself understood to them by shouting, they walked so fast and did not stop. 'Business!' they called back, laughing. 'Where?' — 'At the inn.' — 'I'm going there too!' K. suddenly shouted, louder than all the others; he had a great desire to be taken along by the two. Their acquaintance did not seem to promise much, but they were evidently good, cheerful companions for the road. They heard K.'s words, but only nodded, and were already past.
paras.uz: K. esa tez orada ko'chada turardi, erkaklar uni ostonadan kuzatib turishardi. Yana qor yog'ayotgan edi; shunga qaramay, biroz yorug'roqdek tuyulardi. To'la soqolli toqatsizlik bilan qichqirdi: «Qayerga bormoqchisiz? Bu yo'l Qasrga, bu yo'l qishloqqa olib boradi.» K. unga javob bermadi, lekin ustunligiga qaramay muomalaliroq tuyulgan ikkinchisiga dedi: «Kimsiz? Dam olganim uchun kimga minnatdorchilik bildirishim kerak?» — «Men ko'nchilik ustasi Lazemanman, — degan javob bo'ldi, — lekin hech kimga minnatdor bo'lishingiz shart emas.» — «Yaxshi, — dedi K., — balki yana uchrasharmiz.» — «Unday deb o'ylamayman», dedi erkak. Shu lahzada to'la soqolli qo'lini ko'tarib qichqirdi: «Xayrli kun, Artur, xayrli kun, Yeremiya!» K. o'girildi — demak, bu qishloqda ko'chada odamlar baribir ko'rinar ekan! Qasr tomondan o'rta bo'yli, ikkalasi ham juda xipcha, tor kiyimli, yuzlari ham bir-biriga juda o'xshash ikki yigit kelardi. Ularning yuz rangi to'q jigarrang edi, shunga qaramay uchli soqollari o'zgacha qoraligi bilan ajralib turardi. Ular bunday yo'l sharoitida hayratlanarli darajada tez yurishar, xipcha oyoqlarini bir maromda otishardi. «Nima ishlaring bor?» — qichqirdi to'la soqolli. Ular bilan faqat qichqirib gaplashish mumkin edi — shunchalik tez yurishar va to'xtashmasdi. «Ishlarimiz!» — deb kulib javob qaytarishdi. «Qayerda?» — «Mehmonxonada.» — «Men ham o'sha yoqqa ketyapman!» — deb birdan hammadan baland qichqirdi K.; ikkovi uni o'zlari bilan olib ketishlarini juda istadi; ularning tanishuvi unchalik foydali ko'rinmasa-da, ular, aftidan, yaxshi, quvnoq yo'ldoshlar edi. Ular K.ning so'zlarini eshitishdi, lekin faqat bosh irg'ashdi va allaqachon o'tib ketishdi.

quiz.q: What does K. claim to be when he is woken at night?
o: The land surveyor sent for by the Count
quiz.why_uz: U o'zini graf chaqirgan yer o'lchovchi deb ataydi.

quiz.q: How does the Castle answer on the telephone?
o: First it denies, then confirms him as land surveyor
quiz.why_uz: Avval «yer o'lchovchi yo'q», keyin «xato» — uni tan oladi.
